'''Club Atlético Osasuna''' ({{IPA|es|ˈkluβ aðˈletiko osaˈsuna|lang}}, ''Osasuna Athletic Club''), or simply '''Osasuna''' or '''CAO''', is a Spanish professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Pamplona]], [[Navarre]]. It was founded on 24 October 1920 and plays in [[La Liga]], the top division of Spanish football. The team's home ground is the 23,516-capacity [[El Sadar Stadium]].<ref name="Information of the stadium">{{Cite web|url=https://www.osasuna.es/club/instalaciones/estadio-el-sadar|title=Information of the stadium|website=osasuna.es|language=es|access-date=10 July 2021|archive-date=27 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327145444/https://www.osasuna.es/club/instalaciones/estadio-el-sadar|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

[[File:Estadio El Sadar.jpg|right|300px|thumb|CA Osasuna home stadium's El Sadar.]]

Osasuna is the sole Navarrese club to have played in La Liga. Although the club has never won a national trophy, it reached the Copa del Rey final in [[2005 Copa del Rey Final|2005]] and [[2023 Copa del Rey final|2023]]. The club's best league finishes were fourth in [[1990–91 La Liga|1990–91]] and [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06]].

The team's regular home kit is a red shirt with navy blue shorts. "Los Rojillos" or "Gorritxoak" is the club nickname, meaning "The Little Reds". The word "''osasuna''" means "health" in [[Basque language|Basque]], used in a sense of "strength" or "vigour", which makes Osasuna the only team in La Liga with a Basque name. ==History==

{{Recentism|date=February 2020}}
The club was founded on 24 October 1920 and its name, Osasuna, meaning ''health'' in [[Basque language|Basque]], was chosen by Benjamín Andoian Martínez.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Historia – Inicios|url=https://www.osasuna.es/club/historia|access-date=3 December 2020|website=CA Osasuna Official Website|language=es}}</ref> When Spanish football became professional in 1928, Osasuna was placed in the third division, gaining promotion to the [[Segunda División]] after the [[1931–32 Tercera División|1931–32 season]] by winning the playoff against [[CD Nacional de Madrid|Nacional de Madrid]]. They made it to [[La Liga]] [[1934–35 Segunda División|three seasons later]]. That same season, they reached the semi-finals of the [[1935 Copa del Presidente de la República|Copa del Rey]] and lost to [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. The [[1936 Copa del Presidente de la República|next season]], Osasuna reached the semi-finals again, this time losing to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] over two legs, despite grabbing a victory in the first leg.

The club was hit hard by the [[Navarre#Republic and military uprising|rearguard repression]] implemented by the Nationalist rebels in the [[Spanish coup of July 1936|1936 coup-de-état]] against the Spanish Second Republic. At least ten players, employees and directive board members were murdered, imprisoned or otherwise persecuted.<ref name="Golpe">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2021-05-21|title=El Gobierno de Navarra rinde homenaje a las personas vinculadas a Osasuna represaliadas tras el golpe de 1936|trans-title=The Government of Navarra pays tribute to the people linked to Osasuna who faced retaliations after the 1936 coup|url=https://www.europapress.es/navarra/noticia-gobierno-navarra-rinde-homenaje-personas-vinculadas-osasuna-represaliadas-golpe-1936-20210521133755.html|access-date=2021-05-26|website=Europapress.es}}</ref> The surviving members were forcibly recruited for the front, with some of them showing enthusiasm for the putsch. The strong support of Navarre for the Nationalist rebels led to Osasuna being offered a place in the [[1939–40 La Liga]] when official competitions resumed, although they had finished last in [[1935–36 La Liga|1935–36]] and should have been relegated;<ref>{{Cite web|title='Osasuna 1936. Golpistas, represaliados y franquismo'|trans-title=Osasuna 1936. Coup plotters, reprisals and Francoism|url=https://nuevatribuna.publico.es/articulo/cultura---ocio/entrevista-autores-osasuna-1936-golpistas-represaliados-fascismo-victor-moreno-fernando-miquelarena/20210322175534185917.html|date =23 March 2021|access-date=26 May 2021|website=Nuevatribuna|language=es}}</ref> ultimately a play-off was arranged with the other demoted team [[Atlético Madrid|Atlético Aviación]] – associated with the [[Spanish Air Force]] and thus favoured by the military regime. The [[Madrid]] team won the tie and, with support from their powerful backers, went on to claim the league title and retain it.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Real Madrid and the Metropolitan (2nd part)|trans-title=Real Madrid and the Metropolitan (2nd part)|url=https://www.lagalerna.com/real-madrid-metropolitano-2a-parte/|access-date=29 May 2021|date =10 September 2018|website= La Galerna|language=es}}</ref> It would not be until [[1953–54 La Liga|1953–54]] that Osasuna again participated in the top division, and [[1956–57 La Liga|1956–57]] when they managed to keep their place among the elite, remaining there for three further years.

In September 1967, Osasuna's [[El Sadar Stadium]] was opened with a match between Osasuna and [[Vitoria de Setubal]], with the hosts winning 3–0.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Estadio El Sadar|url=https://www.osasuna.es/club/instalaciones/estadio-el-sadar|access-date=2020-12-07|website=Estadio El Sadar {{!}} CA Osasuna Official Website|language=es|archive-date=27 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327145444/https://www.osasuna.es/club/instalaciones/estadio-el-sadar|url-status=dead}}</ref> The club achieved its first ever [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] qualification in [[1985–86 UEFA Cup|1985–86]] after [[1984–85 La Liga|finishing sixth in the league]]; their campaign began in the first round, eliminating Scottish club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] before being knocked out by Belgian club [[KSV Waregem|Waregem]] 3–2 on aggregate. In the [[1990–91 La Liga|1990–91 season]], Osasuna finished fourth in the league, their best ever league finish until then. This gave them qualification for the [[1991–92 UEFA Cup|following season's UEFA Cup]], where the club reached the third round by eliminating [[Slavia Sofia]] and [[VfB Stuttgart|Stuttgart]]. Finishing last in [[1993–94 La Liga|1993–94]], the side spent six years in the second level, before finally being promoted in [[1999–2000 Segunda División|1999–2000]] after placing 2nd in the league table.
[[File:Club Atlético Osasuna league performance 1929-present.svg|thumb|Chart of CA Osasuna league performance 1929–present]]
In the [[2002–03 Copa del Rey]], Osasuna reached the semi-finals for the first time since 1988. The team entered the competition in the Round of 64, where they beat [[SD Lemona|Lemona]]. In the following rounds, they beat [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], [[Real Unión]] and Sevilla, until the semi-finals where they were knocked out after losing to [[Recreativo de Huelva]] 4–2 on aggregate.

In [[2005 Copa del Rey Final|2005]], they reached the Copa del Rey final for the first time, losing to [[Real Betis]] after [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancup05.html|title=Spain Cup Tournaments 2004/05|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2 May 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907194237/http://www.rsssf.com/tabless/spancup05.html|archive-date=7 September 2008|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="copa051">{{cite web|url=http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/30850/0/FUTBOL/COPADELREY/BETIS/|title=El Betis derrota al Osasuna y se hace con la Copa del Rey|trans-title=Betis defeats Osasuna and wins the Copa del Rey|language=es|publisher=20minutos|date=12 June 2005|access-date=10 January 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180111110211/http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/30850/0/FUTBOL/COPADELREY/BETIS/|archive-date=11 January 2018|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="copa052">{{cite web|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/envivo/2004-2005/junio/osasuna_betis.html|title=Copa del Rey 2004/2005 |language=es|publisher=El Mundo|date=11 June 2005 |access-date=10 January 2018}}</ref> They had a tough campaign in [[2004–05 Copa del Rey|that season's Copa Del Rey]], almost being eliminated in the round of 64 but narrowly beating [[Segunda División B]] side [[CD Castellón|Castellón]] on penalties after a goalless draw. They went on to beat [[Girona FC|Girona]] 1–0 in extra time, then Getafe, Sevilla and [[Atlético Madrid|Atletico Madrid]] each by just one goal difference on aggregate to get to the final.

On 27 November 2005, Osasuna played their 1,000th game in La Liga. After a stellar [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06 domestic campaign]], they made history by finishing in fourth place – equalling the best-ever finish – to enter the [[2006–07 UEFA Champions League|qualifying]] phase for the [[UEFA Champions League]] in the following season. This achievement was made more dramatic by the suspense that was maintained until the last day of the championship in which Osasuna and [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] were both vying for fourth place – both eventually ended the season with the same number of points but Osasuna finished higher due to their head-to-head record. However, they did not make it to the Champions League group phase, after being eliminated by [[Hamburger SV]] in the third qualifying round, leaving the [[Navarre]]se to compete in the UEFA Cup for the fifth time.

[[File:Deporosasuna2.JPG|thumb|Osasuna playing against [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo]] in 2012]]
Osasuna were drawn in Group D of the [[2006–07 UEFA Cup]], and qualified for the knockout stage after finishing second in the group. In the Round of 32, they and were drawn against [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], progressing 1–0 on aggregate, drawing 0–0 away before winning 1–0 in Pamplona through an extra time winner by [[Javad Nekounam]]. Osasuna's next opponent was Rangers, and Osasuna again progressed following a 1–1 draw in [[Glasgow]] and a 1–0 win at home. The club was drawn against German side [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in the quarter-finals. Regarded as severe underdogs, Osasuna not only progressed to the semi-finals but did so in style (a 3–0 away win had virtually sealed the tie, but the ''Rojillos'' also won the second leg, 1–0). In the semi-finals, the club was drawn against [[2005–06 UEFA Cup|holders]] and fellow Spanish side Sevilla, eventually losing 1–2 on aggregate after a 1–0 home win.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Historia – Temporada 2006/07|url=https://www.osasuna.es/club/historia|access-date=3 December 2020|website=CA Osasuna Official Website}}</ref>

In the following two seasons, Osasuna struggled heavily in the league. In [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]], they finished 17th and only one point above relegation. In [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09]], they only avoided relegation in the final day; being in 18th place and entering the final matchday at home to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], the club fell behind but came back with two goals (the decider courtesy of [[Juanfran (footballer, born 1985)|Juanfran]], a ''Merengue'' youth graduate) to beat 9-men ''Los Blancos'' and remain in the top flight by finishing 15th.<ref>{{Cite web|date=31 May 2009|title=Osasuna vs Real Madrid 2–1 La Liga 2008/2009|url=https://www.football-lineups.com/match/50114/|access-date=2020-12-07|website=Football-Lineups}}</ref>

Osasuna had great success in [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]], finishing seventh and one place away from qualifying for the European places, but struggled again in the next 2 seasons, finishing 16th in [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13]] and being relegated to the second division after an 18th-place finish in [[2013–14 La Liga|2013–14]]. In the [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15]] season, the club managed to end up one position above the relegation zone. A managerial change resulted in substantial improvement, and Osasuna won the final match of the regular [[2015–16 Segunda División|2015–16 season]] 0–5 away to [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]], finishing sixth in the table and qualifying for promotion playoffs and. They subsequently won all the playoff games – against [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]] in the semi-final and [[Girona FC|Girona]] in the final – to achieve promotion to La Liga once again. Osasuna finished [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17]] in 19th position, resulting in relegation. They could only manage 8th in their [[2017–18 Segunda División|first campaign]] back in the second tier.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

On 20 May 2019, Osasuna achieved promotion back to La Liga after [[Granada CF|Granada]]'s victory over [[Albacete Balompié|Albacete]], mathematically ensuring a promotion place with three matches left in the season. On 31 May, they defeated [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]] to finish as [[2018–19 Segunda División]] champions.<ref name=arcangel>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/cronica/2019/05/31/5cf18bce268e3e466a8b45a4.html|title=Osasuna, campeón en la Feria de El Arcángel|trans-title=Osasuna, champion in the Fair of the El Arcángel|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=31 May 2019|access-date=1 June 2019}}</ref>

The club celebrated its centenary in October 2020 with a league victory over Athletic Bilbao, albeit the match was played in an empty stadium owing to restrictions caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20201023/484235408571/navarros-frente-al-centenario-de-osasuna.html?facet=amp| title=Navarros frente al centenario de Osasuna|trans-title=Facing up to Navarrese in the Osasuna centenary|newspaper=La Vanguardia|language=es|date=23 October 2020|access-date=25 February 2021}}</ref> In May 2021, after decades of silence and alongside other Navarrese institutions, club president [[Luis Sabalza]] paid homage for the first time to the members who went through the rearguard Nationalist repression during the [[Spanish Civil War]], on behalf of the board of directors.<ref name="Golpe"/>

In 2023, having qualified on the field for the [[UEFA Conference League]] via a [[2022–23 La Liga|7th-place finish]] in La Liga (they also reached the [[2023 Copa del Rey final]], but lost to Real Madrid), Osasuna found itself embroiled in match-fixing allegations<ref>{{Cite news  |date=2023-07-04 |title=Osasuna barred from UEFA Conference League over historic match-fixing scandal |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/osasuna-barred-uefa-conference-league-over-historic-match-fixing-scandal-club-2023-07-04/ |access-date=2023-07-28}}</ref> dating back to 2013, which led to an initial ban from participating (this being the first occasion they had been eligible for a UEFA competition since the events). The club decided to appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), who ruled in their favour in deeming that the club was sufficiently distinct from the directors who committed the offences<ref>{{cite web |title=Osasuna cleared to play in Conference League playoff round |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/osasuna-cleared-play-conference-league-playoff-round-2023-07-25/ |website=Reuters |access-date=29 July 2023 |language=en |date=25 July 2023}}</ref> and reinstated their access to the Conference League. UEFA also initiated a disciplinary case against Osasuna for taking the matter to civil courts.

== Rivalries ==
Osasuna has many rivalries: these include Real Zaragoza, Real Madrid,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> and Athletic Bilbao.

The rivalry with Real Madrid began in December 1990, when Osasuna won 4–0 at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]].<ref name=":1" /> The rivalry with Zaragoza wasn't always a heated rivalry, but hostility between the two clubs began during a match in October 1987, when Zaragoza fans threw an object at Osasuna goalkeeper [[Roberto Santamaría (footballer, born 1962)|Roberto Santamaría]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Noticias|first=Diario de|date=23 February 2019|title=El eterno rival|url=https://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/osasuna/2019/02/23/eterno-rival/810543.html|access-date=2022-02-16|website=Noticias de Navarra|language=es}}</ref> Since then, these matches often have altercations between fans and players, and it is known to be one of the most heated rivalries in Spain.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pascual|first=Maider|date=20 February 2019|title=Rivalidad histórica entre Osasuna y Zaragoza|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2019/02/19/osasuna/969368-rivalidad-historica-entre-osasuna-y-zaragoza.html|access-date=2022-02-16|website=VAVEL|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-06-30|title=Osasuna – Zaragoza, historia de una rivalidad|url=http://wanderersfutbol.com/osasuna-zaragoza-historia-de-una-rivalidad|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190922182427/http://wanderersfutbol.com/osasuna-zaragoza-historia-de-una-rivalidad|url-status=usurped|archive-date=22 September 2019|access-date=2022-02-16|website=Wanderersfutbol|language=es}}</ref>  In recent years however, there have been large periods of time where this rivalry match wasn't played, due to the clubs being in different divisions.
